headline: Tokyo inflation keeps a BoJ hike in play as Wall Street returns for a half-day

findings.headline: Tokyo core inflation jumps on energy, but the underlying measure cools
findings.body: Tokyo core CPI (ex fresh food) rose 2.9% y/y in November from 2.6%, a shade under the 3.0% expected, as the end of electricity and gas subsidies pushed energy up. The measure excluding fresh food and energy, which the Bank of Japan watches for underlying inflation, eased to 2.5% from 2.6%. That keeps a December BoJ hike in play without forcing it, so the yen and JGB yields stay sensitive to BoJ guidance into the meeting.

findings.headline: Altria confirms it is weighing a cash bid for Imperial Brands
findings.body: Altria said it is considering a possible offer for Imperial Brands, likely all in cash, and is in talks with a third party, reported by Bloomberg to be Japan Tobacco, about buying part of Imperial's business. Under UK takeover rules Altria must make a firm offer or walk away by 24 December. It is the first large tobacco consolidation move in years and puts a bid floor under Imperial when London opens, while Japan Tobacco's role makes a carve-up by region the likely shape.

findings.headline: OPEC+ leans towards rolling quotas into January, with the audit still disputed
findings.body: Delegates say OPEC+ is considering keeping current production quotas into January at Sunday's 29 November meeting. The harder argument is over the capacity audit that sets 2027 baselines, with Iraq objecting, and Gulf supply disruptions from the Iran war cloud any assessment. A rollover would leave the Hormuz and Saudi-attack premium as the main driver of crude, so a surprise on baselines is the bigger risk for next week.

view: Our view: Overnight was a continuation, not a new story. Asia keeps buying back the chip selloff and US futures point to a firmer reopening, but Wall Street's half-day session (closing 19:00 Zurich) is a thin test. The real decisions sit next week with OPEC+ on Sunday and the BoJ in December.
